text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributes 0.75 to each of 4 members, making full contribution socially optimal even though individually keeping tokens is the dominant strategy. Given it's a 10-round repeated game, I'll open cooperatively and contribute all 20.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: Each token contributed to the group returns 0.75 to each of 4 members, meaning 3 total per token versus keeping 1 individually—so while self-interest favors keeping tokens, full cooperation maximizes group welfare. Since this is a repeated 10-round game, I'm leaning toward starting with a high contribution to signal cooperative intent, while staying open to adjusting based on others' behavior.
